newsitem.title: UK: North Sea crudes rise as some grades sold out.
newsitem.headline: North Sea crudes rise as some grades sold out.

text.p: North Sea physical differentials firmed, with gas oil-rich Oseberg fetching a sharply higher premium as a mountain of Brent cargoes began to move steadily and other grades were sold out for early October, traders said.

A Brent maximum cargo loading in first decade October traded at a firmer November +12 cents, up from Wednesday's average of November +3 cents. A million barrels of Brent was also sold at November +7 cents earlier in the day. A U.K. major, who kept one of the two Brent dates on Thursday, now holds only four Brent cargoes out of nine it held last week. A trader kept the second Oct 11-13 Brent date.

Northwest European refiners began a huge buying spree on Tuesday, clearing out all but a handful of North Sea grades for Oct 1-10. Rumoured sales of Forties and Ekofisk into the Med have not been confirmed.

With little else on offer, Norwegian Oseberg commanded a sharply higher premium of 35 cents over Dated Brent with two mid-October cargoes moving at that level, up 10 cents on Tuesday's deals. "I don't think there's much available and Brent is clearing up, so I would say the market is much more solid," a wet trader said.
"The difference between the picture now and a week ago is the difference between night and day," he added. "It's a much more solid picture."

Intermonth paper spreads were also slightly firmer with Oct/Nov moving up to talk around +42/+44 cents from +34/+40 earlier in the day. Forward spreads were steady to firm at +53/+56 cents for Nov/Dec and +60/+61 cents for Dec/Jan.
CFDs were also talked higher in line with firmer physical deals, with next week's dates assessed at Nov +9/+12 cents.
